data.title: Panel calls MP Suchada and husband
data.description: People's Party (PP) MP Rangsiman Rome has called Bhumjaithai MP Suchada Zhang Thaensap and her husband to testify before a House committee on Wednesday over allegations involving online gambling and money laundering.

data.title: 'Gambler' Hudson ready to roll the dice once again
data.description: Thailand coach Anthony Hudson, pressed over his rotation policy, says he would make the same gamble again as his men face hosts Indonesia in tonight's inaugural Fifa Asean Cup final.

data.title: Govt defends 'sin tax' funding shake-up
data.description: The government has defended proposed changes to the funding of four state bodies, rejecting claims that they would lower alcohol and tobacco taxes or benefit producers.

data.title: Flood plans on ice over red tape
data.description: Nearly a decade after Thailand drew up a 500-billion-baht plan to overhaul its flood management system, most of the nine projects remain unfinished, with budget constraints and opposition to land expropriation slowing progress.

data.title: Flooding forces 50 health facilities to halt services
data.description: Flooding has affected 141 healthcare facilities in 18 provinces, forcing 50 to suspend services. A total of 319 roads have also been affected.

data.title: Flood diversion plan faces scrutiny
data.description: The 160-billion-baht Chai Nat–Pasak–Gulf of Thailand water-diversion project has come under renewed scrutiny after the cabinet approved the scheme, which the government says will reduce flood risks across the Chao Phraya Basin.

data.title: NGO urges Türkiye to end  raids on LGBTQ+ people
data.description: Apcom Foundation, a Thai-based rights group, has called on Türkiye to end a crackdown on LGBTQI+ people, health workers and civil society groups following more than 100 arrests since Sept 12.

data.title: Unfiltered cinema
data.description: Thamuya Thasananukulkij's first feature film echoes their childhood. They did not want to do what is told, but did not dare to speak up. They could neither fathom nor describe muddy feelings under the surface until they saw a herd of cattle at a friend's house in Suphan Buri, which seemed to understand everything, but could not speak human language. They were interested in how caretakers tame children and animals.

data.title: Newin wishes PM 2 more terms
data.description: Bhumjaithai Party heavyweight Newin Chidchob wished Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul another two terms in office, or until he grew tired of the job, as he celebrated his 68th birthday in Buri Ram on Sunday.

data.title: Bosnian Serb strongman claims election win, thanks Trump and Putin
data.description: SARAJEVO - The former president of Bosnia's Serb statelet, Milorad Dodik, said his party had retained power in the entity and its seat on the shared presidency, as preliminary results showed a drop in turnout for Bosnia's general elections.

data.title: Cyclists turn Nagoya blank into fuel for Olympic push
data.description: Thailand's cyclists leave the Asian Games in Nagoya without a medal, but with a sharper sense of what it will take to reach the 2028 Olympics, and with enough ranking points banked to keep realistic hopes alive on road, track and BMX.

data.title: Eighteen gold, and a record away haul
data.description: Thailand arrived in Nagoya with a target of 14 gold medals. They left with 18, and a place in the record books.

data.title: Israel wear black armbands in Ireland tie over Hamas attack
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israel's national football team wore black armbands in their Nations League clash against Ireland on Sunday to commemorate the victims of Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack, after Irish players wore them to protest the war in Gaza.

data.title: Teen titans shine in chaotic Games
data.description: NAGOYA: The 20th Asian Games closed yesterday after a rocky fortnight lit up by youthful brilliance in the sporting arenas but tempered by ‌logistical dysfunction and subdued public interest.

data.title: Indians protest election chief ahead of top court hearing
data.description: NEW DELHI - Indian opposition activists rallied for a third day on Sunday to demand the election commission chief's resignation, alleging wrongdoing during a large-scale revision of voter rolls in the world's largest democracy.

data.title: Up to 500 French schools to be totally or partly closed Monday: minister
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Up to 500 schools across France will be totally or partly closed on Monday because of a wave of student protests that has shaken the country, the education minister said.

data.title: Trump confirms national intelligence chief as new AI czar
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump on Sunday confirmed national intelligence chief Jay Clayton as head of a new White House task force on artificial intelligence, amid increasingly vocal warnings from researchers about the technology's potential dangers.

data.title: Iran tells US there is no military solution to Middle East war
data.description: TEHRAN - Iran's top diplomat insisted on Sunday that there would be no military solution to the United States' war against the Islamic republic, with talks on ending the conflict apparently at an impasse.

data.title: UK Green party adopts 'Zionism is racism' policy
data.description: LONDON - The UK's left-wing Green party on Sunday voted to define Zionism as racism at the party's annual get-together, drawing sharp backlash from British Jewish groups and the Israeli government.

data.title: Ethiopia controls Tigray capital as regional rivals meet in Egypt
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Ethiopian federal forces were in full control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, a local journalist said Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.

data.title: University gifts 3,000 long-life meals to flood-hit communities
data.description: Prince of Songkla University (PSU) has delivered 3,000 boxes of ready-to-eat meals developed under its “Grab agro” brand to Silpakorn University, for distribution to people affected by the flooding.

data.title: Drainage slow, but no risk of fresh flooding, says Bangkok governor
data.description: The flood is draining slowly in eastern Bangkok, but the good news is forecasts indicate there is no immediate risk of fresh flooding from rain or the runoff-surge coming from the North, Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said on Sunday.
